title: CombiFlow: Flow cytometry-based identification and characterization of genetically and functionally distinct AML subclones
protocol: Thaw two tubes of 6 mL newborn calf serum (NCS).
Collect the AML sample from liquid nitrogen storage.
Quickly thaw the AML sample in a water bath at 37°C.
Transfer the AML sample to an NCS tube and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 450 g.
Prepare NCS mix by adding heparin, MgSO4, and DNAse I to another NCS tube.
Resuspend the AML cell pellet in pre-warmed NCS mix.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Spin down cells and resuspend in PBS-mix (6 mL PBS + DNAse and MgSO4).
Count viable cells using Trypan Blue.
Run the marker panel or sort potential subclones.
Take 15 million viable mononuclear cells (MNCs) of the thawed AML sample and resuspend this in 320 μL PBS.
Add 2 μL of cell suspension to the unstained and single stained control tubes containing 98 μL PBS.
Add FcR blocking reagent 10 μL, CD34-APC 9 μL, CD38-FITC 9 μL, CD45-PECy7 3 μL, and CD45RA-BV421 3 μL to the remaining cells.
Stain cells for 20 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add PBS to the backbone-stained cells in a total volume of 100 μL multiplied by the number of markers.
Add 100 μL of backbone-stained cells to each labeled tube.
Resuspend the tubes to ensure an even distribution of cells.
Pipette one PE-labeled plasma membrane protein marker antibody per tube according to the key resources table.
Incubate the cells for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of PBS per tube and centrifuge at 450 g for 5 minutes.
Remove the PBS and resuspend the cells in 100 μL fresh PBS.
Acquire expression data using a flow cytometer.
Gate the FCS files in FlowJo.
Export the cells of interest as new FCS files.
Combine FlowJo™ exported FCS files into a merged file using Infinicyt™.
Load all FCS files necessary for your analysis within the Infinicyt™ environment.
Select ‘Calculate data’ in the ‘Guided modules’ window.
Deselect parameters that can be excluded, such as the time parameter HDR-TSeparate the PE parameter so that one row is created for every included marker
Check for a potential merge warning.
Check out troubleshooting – problem 1 if this is the case
Rename the rows that were created by the corresponding plasma membrane protein marker name
Check the “The selected populations were unequivocally identified” box and select calculate data
Save the calculated data file before continuing to the analysis window
Continue to the analysis window and save
Export the merged FCS file
Export marker expression data per cell from the population of interest in the merged FCS file using FlowJo™.
Prepare a data file for the healthy control.
Run R script: “Marker panel – histograms” to plot plasma membrane protein marker expression data.
Save generated histogram plot as pdf.
Select plasma membrane protein markers that are aberrantly expressed in comparison to the healthy control using the previously generated histogram plots.
Open the analysis file, saved in step 13i, in the Infinicyt™ environment.
If necessary: gate population of interest.
Check if Negative Visibility Configuration is selected for Automatic Negativity.
Perform a Principal Component analysis.
Plot an APS (Automated Population Separator) diagram (Ctrl+D).
Deselect backbone markers and select aberrantly expressed markers (Right click: Diagram Configuration → Parameters Configuration).
Obtain Principal Component values (Ctrl+I) and select most distinguishing markers.
Gate subpopulations and visualize in dot plots.
Export all graphs and individual subpopulations for use in Manuscript Figures or downstream analysis.
Determine a sorting strategy using the most distinguishing marker(s) in the merged FCS file using Flow Jo™.
Continue with Sorting of potential subclones.
Label tubes for unstained and single stained controls.
Resuspend all thawed AML cells in PBS-mix (10 × 10^6 cells/100 μL).
Add 1 ul of cells to unstained and single stained controls containing 99 μL of PBS-mix.
Stain remaining cells with CD34-APC, CD45-PECy7, PMP marker 1-PE, and optionally PMP marker 2.
Incubate stained cells for 20 min at 4°C.
Wash cells with PBS and resuspend them in ±300 μL PBS-mix.
Add PI stain to the main tube at 1 μg/mL in 1000 μL PBS-mix per 50 × 10^6 cells.
Sort subclones of interest from the stained sample.
Check troubleshooting for FACS sorter clogging if necessary.
Process sorted cells for downstream analysis such as targeted sequencing, RNA sequencing, or culturing.
Export population of interest from the merged FCS files using FlowJo™.
Zip the exported files.
Create a metadata file.
Create a panel file.
Create a cluster file.
Create a heatmap that depicts transformed marker expression per cluster.
Assign clusters to specific cell types using the heatmap.
Run the script until the step ‘Manual clustering per sample’.
Assign clusters to samples based on the cluster cell count per sample.
Create a sample file for each sample.
Visualize newly assigned clusters for all samples combined or per sample.
Create a new heatmap depicting the combined expression of all clusters assigned to one specific sample.
Select markers and clusters to include in Principal Component analysis.
Perform Principal Component analysis for all included samples.
Optionally, perform Principal Component analysis comparing diagnosis and relapse without healthy clusters.
Run Principal Component analysis to identify the most discriminating marker(s).
Create a file similar to the cluster and sample file but assign each cluster to a cell type based on expression data in the heatmap.
Assign clusters with small size, high CD45 and CD19 expression specifically to B cells or lymphocytes.
Assign cells from both leukemic and healthy samples to the healthy sample if the ratio of Healthy/Leukemic cells is above 1:8.
